catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class fits a typed nav_msgs/OccupancyGrid read. cap.world.state.v1 requires a canonical state_hash and revision that the message does not carry; cap.sensing.read.v1 requires an RFC 3339 sampled_at string and a generic values object, not the typed grid.

No catalogue class fits a headerless ros_autonomous_slam/PointArray of clustered frontier targets. cap.sensing.point_cloud.v1 requires a PointCloud2 artifact and point_count; PointArray has no header, no artifact and no frame.

No catalogue class fits one operator-published geometry_msgs/PointStamped boundary point. cap.sensing.read.v1 is generic and requires an RFC 3339 sampled_at string; the RRT region is an ordered set of points, not one sensor channel.
No catalogue class fits a typed nav_msgs/Odometry read. cap.sensing.read.v1 is generic and requires an RFC 3339 sampled_at string; cap.sensing.imu.v1 has a different fixed schema and is not odometry.

No catalogue class fits a typed sensor_msgs/LaserScan read. cap.sensing.point_cloud.v1 requires a PointCloud2 artifact and point_count; cap.sensing.read.v1 is generic and requires an RFC 3339 sampled_at string, not typed ranges and angles.

notes:
PASS on the fake backend only; the gate reports evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. This package is model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 with run_id ros-wave-c-061, and reviewed_by stays null. No human reviewed or tested anything, no hardware was attached, and no ROS graph, rosbridge connection, Gazebo process, GMAPPING, move_base, RRT node or upstream simulator run is claimed.

RECON AND SCOPE: The pinned repository is a ROS 1 catkin task environment. It has no Python native class; this is a configuration-only RosDriver and native.py is not used. No preflight section for this exact package and pin is present in the two named ros-wave-b PREFLIGHT.md files. The upstream nodes publish /cmd_vel, publish /filtered_points (ros_autonomous_slam/PointArray), subscribe /map, /odom and /scan, subscribe /clicked_point (geometry_msgs/PointStamped), and call the external /move_base action. The RRT detectors require five ordered /clicked_point points (README.md:34-35; src/global_rrt_detector.cpp:81,132-175). This package binds five explicit fresh-subscription observations: /map (nav_msgs/OccupancyGrid), /filtered_points (PointArray), /clicked_point (PointStamped), /odom (nav_msgs/Odometry) and /scan (sensor_msgs/LaserScan). Each is an explicit observation action, not an automatic resource snapshot; the main resource snapshot is empty, so a silent topic fails only the observation that asked for it.

CONTROL LIMITATION: This is an observation profile, not a motion-control driver. It deliberately does not publish /clicked_point, /cmd_vel or /move_base goals. The five /clicked_point messages start autonomous RRT exploration, and the upstream registers no acknowledged stop service or action; a zero-velocity publication and action cancellation are not accepted stop bindings. NOT COVERED: operator motion control, exploration start, navigation and any stop or safe state. A full control integration remains blocked on the missing acknowledged stop contract; if the orchestrator requires that control surface, this card should be treated as HELPER_MISSING rather than accepting the observation profile as full task control. The map is produced by the external SLAM stack (gmapping/map_server) or the optional a_star_main.py publisher; the explorer subscribes to the same topic, and this package does not prove the publisher is running.

FAKE: The card preferred upstream-sim, but the pinned ROS 1/Gazebo/Catkin stack is not installed and this task forbids network and pip install; the checked backend is a package-local ROS-free canned transport, not the upstream simulator and not a recording. It claims F0, runs no physics or pacing, no GMAPPING, RRT, wall-following, move_base or wall-clock loop, and has no reset or snapshot. All values are placeholders: a 4 by 3 map with 12 cells, 3 frontier points, one region point and 8 scan ranges/intensities. The live map size is the OccupancyGrid width times height, the live frontier count is the filtered cluster count, wall_follow.py loops over 360 scan bins, and the RRT nodes allocate 384 by 384 map buffers (nodes/autonomous_rrt.py:24); these are code assumptions, not bounds. NOT COVERED: the full live map and scan arrays, TF, sensor timing, QoS, Gazebo physics and contacts, GMAPPING, the RRT and wall-follow loops, move_base, /cmd_vel and the full /clicked_point region sequence.

SAFETY: risk R0 because every bound capability is a read observation of simulated task state and no actuation capability is bound. A stock e-stop is software-only and latches the extension reads (they have no catalogue-read exemption); there is no native stop, world pause or physical safe state in this profile. This is not a hardware e-stop claim. No site-limits.example.json is needed because the profile has no numeric input and declares no Limit.

CHECKS: G1-G7 and G9 pass; the only warning is G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE because no actuating capability has a limit to probe. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised. test_driver.py keeps check_driver and adds eleven repository cases: the five observations, the pinned endpoint/type pairs, silent and unrelated-id subscriptions, malformed messages through the stock server, the absence of any actuation operation, and the software-only e-stop latch. The clone was left unmodified; no network, pip install or upstream execution was used.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the five observation endpoints and types (/map and /odom at nodes/autonomous_rrt.py:179-180, /filtered_points at scripts/filter.py:112 with msg/PointArray.msg:3, /scan at nodes/wall_follow.py:61, /clicked_point at src/global_rrt_detector.cpp:81), each output schema against the ROS 1 message definitions (OccupancyGrid, the headerless PointArray, PointStamped, nested Odometry, LaserScan), all 19 facts, the launch files and the R0 observation-only scope (no command, stop or reset is bound; the upstream /cmd_vel publishers and move_base client stay internal). Three defects were fixed: the scan schema said a non-finite range represents no return, but the bridge refuses non-finite numbers, so such a scan fails (reviewer probe), now stated in the field description, a gap and facts.md and covered by a new package case with a fake switch; the operator-only /clicked_point topic (silent unless a point arrives within the 2 s wire default) and the 1 MiB message bound for a live map were undisclosed, now in the gaps and facts.md; and facts.md said wall_follow.py defaults to relative names although it uses the absolute /scan and /cmd_vel (wall_follow.py:60-61). Reviewer changed driver.py, fake.py, test_driver.py (the docstring's subscription count and the non-finite case) and facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json; the gate and collect.py --strict pass with the expected G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE and the digest unchanged, and all 13 tests pass. RESULT.json's 'eleven repository cases' is now twelve. For the human reviewer: Observation-only R0 profile: nothing is commanded and the stock e-stop is software_only. A live deployment of this stack runs autonomous exploration (RRT or wall following publishing /cmd_vel, move_base goals) that this package can neither start nor stop. /map, /odom and /scan carry the same names on a real TurtleBot3, so an endpoint pointed at a real robot would read its sensors. nodes/autonomous_rrt.py (node RRT_Explorer), whose lines the /map and /odom bindings cite, is started by no launch file and reads a hard-coded /home/fazildgr8 image path (autonomous_rrt.py:181).
